parole.testo: From Late Latin compāniō (nominative form), a calque of Proto-West Germanic *gahlaibō. Doublet of compagnone, which came via the Latin accusative compāniōnem.

parole.significato: a type of raviolo, from around Abruzzo, typically eaten at Easter
parole.testo: From Late Latin fladonem, from Proto-West Germanic *flaþō (“flatcake”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Greek φλαούνα (flaoúna, “Cypriot pastry”), English flathe, Dutch vla, vlade (“baked custard, pancake”), Middle Low German vlade (“flatcake”), German Fladen (“a flatcake, cowpatty”). Related to f

parole.significato: to steal (take something belonging to another)
parole.testo: Inherited from Late Latin raubāre, from Proto-West Germanic *raubōn.
